proseChanges.summary: **Managed installation verification:** includes the generator-recorded portable contract anchor. A managed source copy with only its own two installation commits can now run the existing contract check without the publisher's Git history. Setup, build, verification and artifact creation keep their declared checks; this fixes the `contract_anchor_missing` failure after copying v0.4.24. **Unused legacy reservations and attachment custody:** the original installation owner can approve a different package fingerprint after an unused adoption reservation expires, is discarded or pauses with an error, provided no destination workspace was created and no erasure or deletion fence applies. Created provenance remains permanent, and the old fingerprint stays closed. Canonical attachment custody transfers with the unused reservation, including already cleaned coordinates; old cleanup jobs cannot delete a replacement package's live attachments or stop its import wakeups. A cleanup already deleting objects must finish its claim before that handoff. **Clearer imported history and results:** historical staff display as Former staff, while historical contact, AI and system authors retain their distinctions; none gains native membership or assignment authority. Move in shows the actual pause code and a matching explanation, distinguishes historical verification from current source availability, and labels historical memberships as granting no access. Reconciliation tables can be reached and scrolled with the keyboard, including on phones. Imported AI profiles remain disabled and imported workflows stay draft. **Tickets and mailbox setup:** a ticket starting with an internal note can be created before a mailbox is connected, without sending email. Email-first tickets still require a connected mailbox. Email settings explain missing installation prerequisites and local-trial limits, with hosted Google, Microsoft, IMAP/SMTP and forwarding instructions. A local trial sends and receives no email; use website chat to try conversations. Connecting a mailbox does not configure sign-in or invitation mail. Live mailbox/provider qualification remains separate. **Fresh hosted installs:** native setup, ordinary support and the ticket/mailbox guidance above are active. The importer runner and adoption remain inert until a legacy package is imported through the approved flow; cleanup continues for already registered packages. Updating alone starts no import, sends no mail and grants no historical-user access. The corrected mail declaration and rer 0.2.112 are retained. Real-customer remote importer use, signed migration-before-Worker delivery and live-provider qualification remain separate; this preparation authorizes no production import or cutover. **Migrations:** no migrations since v0.4.24. The inventory remains 195 files, byte-identical to v0.4.24, so its applied migration ledger stays unchanged. A v0.4.23 installation applies 328, 329, 331 and 332 once in filename order BEFORE the new Worker serves HTTP or queue traffic; v0.4.22 first applies 327, retaining the published buyer steps. There is no migration 326 or 330.
proseChanges.was: v0.4.24 managed source verification needs unavailable publisher history; unused adoption reservations can block a replacement package and old cleanup can remove its attachments.
proseChanges.now: v0.4.25 records the portable contract anchor, recovers unused reservations with attachment custody retained, clarifies imported history and results, and improves internal-only tickets and mailbox setup guidance. No migration; 195 files remain. Upgrade baselines: v0.4.24, v0.4.23 and v0.4.22. rer remains 0.2.112.
proseChanges.ownerAction: Update from v0.4.24 without resetting; v0.4.23 and v0.4.22 are also upgrade baselines. Back up D1, R2, Durable Object state and private settings first. Use Node 22.20.0, pnpm 10.12.4 and pinned rer 0.2.112. Retain native owners, permissions, support history, files, erasure fences and every applied migration identity. A v0.4.24 installation applies no migration. Stop the old Worker before applying any missing migrations on older installations: v0.4.23 applies 328_legacy_workspace_adoption.sql, 329_legacy_package_custody.sql, 331_legacy_cleanup_seeding.sql and 332_legacy_cleanup_inventory_lazy.sql once in that order BEFORE the new Worker serves HTTP or queue traffic; v0.4.22 first applies 327_legacy_import_worker.sql. Retain those releases' published buyer steps, including 332's conditional cleanup of only an untouched empty inventory marker. Earlier installations first apply every other missing published migration in filename order. There is no migration 326 or 330 in this release. Run `rer deploy --dry-run` against the retained installation before any separately authorized deployment. V1 source stays cleanup-only and must never be relabeled v2; incomplete cleanup remains pending. No reset, mail activation, recovery adoption, production import, cutover or production deployment is part of this preparation.

pendingMigrations.buyerSteps: Back up D1, R2 and private installation encryption custody before updating. Apply 330_identity_recovery.sql once BEFORE the new Worker serves HTTP or queue traffic. On v0.4.24, apply this missing filename even though 331 and 332 are already recorded; retain every applied migration identity. Keep the durable recovery revocation watermark on rollback. Discard live recovery requests, approvals, pending factors and capabilities on restore; rebind Managed custody after a portable restore. This adds scoped first-owner and all-workspace consent recovery state and invalidation triggers without rewriting accounts, factors, memberships or spent-key history. Managed recovery remains unavailable until the separate declaration and custody round enables it. No reset or deployment is authorized.
